h1: FUE Hair Transplant in Huntington Beach
intro: An FUE (follicular unit extraction) hair transplant moves individual hair follicles from the back and sides of the scalp to areas that are thinning or balding. It is typically a fit for men and women with stable pattern hair loss who have enough healthy donor hair. At CAIR SPA in Huntington Beach, it starts with a free consultation to see if you are a candidate.

quickFacts.label: Treatment time
quickFacts.value: Often several hours to a full day, depending on the number of grafts

quickFacts.label: Downtime
quickFacts.value: Many people return to light activity within a few days

quickFacts.label: Results
quickFacts.value: New growth often begins around 3 to 4 months, with fuller results typically by 12 to 18 months

quickFacts.label: Sessions
quickFacts.value: Usually one procedure, though some people choose a second session later

whatIs: In a follicular unit extraction (FUE) transplant, small groups of one to four hairs, called follicular units, are removed one at a time from a donor area where hair is naturally more resistant to thinning. These grafts are then placed into areas of thinning or balding. Because there is no strip of scalp removed, FUE does not leave a long linear scar, though it does leave tiny dot-like scars that are usually hidden by surrounding hair.

Each follicular unit is removed with a very small punch tool, then placed into tiny recipient sites in the thinning area at angles designed to blend with your existing hair. Your hairline design, graft placement and overall plan are set by your provider, and results depend on your donor hair, the pattern of your hair loss and how your body heals. A transplant moves existing hair rather than creating new follicles, and it does not stop future hair loss in untreated areas. All services at CAIR SPA are performed under the oversight of Tran Plastic Surgery, led by Dr. Tuan Tran.
goodFor: Male pattern hair loss with stable, healthy donor hair
Some cases of female pattern hair loss, after evaluation
People who prefer to avoid a linear donor scar
Those who want to wear their hair shorter in back
Restoring density in areas where hair loss has stabilized

steps.title: Consultation
steps.text: Your provider examines your scalp, reviews your hair loss history and health, and evaluates your donor area. You will discuss realistic goals, hairline design and whether an FUE hair transplant is a good fit.

steps.title: Preparation
steps.text: On procedure day the donor area is trimmed short and the scalp is numbed with local anesthesia. Your recipient area and hairline are marked according to your plan.

steps.title: Follicle harvesting
steps.text: Your provider removes follicular units one at a time from the donor area using a tiny punch tool, keeping the extraction spread out so the donor area still looks natural.

steps.title: Graft placement
steps.text: The team creates small recipient sites and places the grafts at angles designed to look natural with your existing hair.

steps.title: Recovery and follow-up
steps.text: You go home with aftercare instructions, and follow-up visits track healing and growth over the coming months.

expect.before: Your provider will give you specific instructions, which may include pausing certain medications or supplements, avoiding alcohol and not smoking before your procedure. Plan for a long appointment, wear a button-up shirt and arrange a ride home.
expect.during: Local anesthesia numbs the scalp, so most people feel pressure rather than pain after the initial numbing injections. You will be awake and can typically rest, listen to music or watch something during breaks.
expect.after: Mild swelling, redness, tenderness and small scabs are common for the first one to two weeks. It is normal for transplanted hairs to shed within the first several weeks before new growth begins. Follow your aftercare instructions for washing, sleeping position and activity to support healing.

faqs.q: How much does an FUE hair transplant cost?
faqs.a: The price depends on the plan, mainly the number of grafts needed for your goals. We give you an exact quote at your free consultation after evaluating your scalp and donor hair.

faqs.q: What is the downtime after an FUE hair transplant?
faqs.a: Many people return to desk work and light activity within a few days, though swelling and scabbing may be visible for about a week or two. Strenuous exercise is usually limited for a short period. Your provider will give you a timeline based on your procedure.

faqs.q: How long do hair transplant results last?
faqs.a: Transplanted follicles are taken from areas that are typically resistant to thinning, so they often continue to grow long term. However, untreated hair around the transplant can keep thinning over time, which is why some people pair a transplant with other hair loss treatments. Results vary by person.

faqs.q: Does an FUE hair transplant hurt?
faqs.a: The numbing injections at the start cause some brief discomfort. After that, most people feel pressure rather than pain during the procedure. Soreness afterward is usually mild and managed with the medication your provider recommends.

faqs.q: Who is a good candidate for an FUE hair transplant?
faqs.a: Good candidates usually have pattern hair loss that has stabilized and enough healthy donor hair at the back and sides of the scalp. People with very limited donor hair, certain scalp conditions or some types of hair loss may not be good candidates. Your provider will assess this at your consultation.

FUE does not leave a long linear scar like strip harvesting does. It leaves very small dot-like scars in the donor area that are typically hard to see once hair grows back, although they may be noticeable with a very close shave. At our Huntington Beach spa, your provider will discuss what to expect for your hair type.
